question: Can the LLDA public biodiversity overview support a Laguna de Bay fish checklist or species assertion?

source.title: Biodiversity of the Laguna de Bay Region
source.pageCitation: The page says its source is the Laguna de Bay Basin Master Plan: 2016 and Beyond.
source.underlyingSourceAccess: Direct linked master-plan PDF request returned HTTP 403; no access control was bypassed.

findings.pageReportedAggregate: 31 fish species, 16 families, and 19 genera for Laguna de Bay.
findings.pageReportedCommercialFishText: The page gives a short common-name list and parenthetical scientific-name strings, but does not expose a 31-row checklist or link those names to dates, methods, samples, stations, or vouchers.
taxonomicAndTextQualityFlags: The parenthetical text includes an apparent OCR or transcription string, 'Anus rnanilensis'; it is preserved here only as a quality flag and is not taxonomically corrected.
Several entries use historical combinations, genus-level labels, or abbreviated names; none was crosswalked into a species assertion in this review.
The page's phrase 'commercially important' is an attributed historical management-context statement, not current abundance, catchability, or fishing advice.
findings.pageImages: The page exposes illustrative images labeled Ayungin, Bighead Carp, Crustacean, and Tilapia. Their individual scientific identifications and reuse licenses were not verified; none was copied or approved for the species-image registry.

rightsReview.termsFinding: No item-specific open-data license or republication grant was identified on the reviewed page.
rightsReview.decision: Do not copy the page's species-name list, text, or images into the app pending source, taxonomy, and item-level rights review.

limits: The LLDA webpage does not state when its content was last updated, the survey dates behind the aggregate, sampling methods, source table, vouchers, or a full scientific-name checklist.
The linked 2016 Basin Master Plan could not be retrieved through the direct URL in this review, so the cited underlying source and its specific fish evidence were not independently checked.
The 31-species figure is an agency-reported aggregate, not a set of independently reviewed species records or a current lake census.
No current-presence, distribution, abundance, catchability, diet, fishing-rule, water-safety, or image-identification claim follows from this review.
nextAction: Seek an independently accessible, dated and rights-cleared Laguna de Bay fish survey or specimen source. Treat the LLDA page as a historical source lead until the cited plan or its underlying evidence can be reviewed.
